title: Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
abstract: arXiv:2411.14013v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. Leveraging the Mahalanobis distance of the residual for a given audio signal to these model-specific fingerprints allows to identify the source model as well as to distinguish real from fake audio. A broad set of experiments across multiple synthesis systems and languages demonstrate a supreme performance of the proposed approach on four tasks: open-world single-model attribution, closed-world multi-model attribution, real vs. synthetic speech classification, and out-of-domain detection.

translated_title: 基于残差统计指纹的合成语音轻量级检测与模型归属识别
translated_abstract: 随着语音生成技术的不断进步，冒充、虚假信息和语音欺骗的风险也随之增加。我们提出了一种轻量级、无需训练的合成语音检测与源模型归属识别方法。该方法基于模型特定的指纹，这些指纹通过计算音频信号与其滤波版本之间差异（称为残差）的平均值来获得。利用给定音频信号的残差与这些模型特定指纹之间的马氏距离，可以识别源模型，并区分真实音频与虚假音频。在多个合成系统和语言上开展的大量实验表明，所提出的方法在四项任务上表现卓越：开放世界单模型归属识别、封闭世界多模型归属识别、真实语音与合成语音分类，以及域外检测。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无需训练的轻量级方法，通过音频残差的统计指纹与马氏距离实现合成语音检测和源模型归属识别，在归属识别、真假分类及域外检测等多项任务上表现卓越。
